scope: Read-only source and receipt review; no graph build, pickle load, compile, sampler, or output mutation
supported: The audit script checks plan/execution receipt hashes, source pins, resource/review pins, stage sequence, first-parent contract, factor inventory, 64 contiguous variable segments totaling 662, and the terminal file-size failure. It stats and hashes the partial pickle in 1 MiB reads and never deserializes it.

Reported 64 MiB exact partial file, OSError file-size cap, process exit 1/no watchdog termination, and post-monitor output accounting are consistent with the recorded terminal and bounded audit methodology. The serialization total is correctly unknown; 64 MiB is only an attempted lower bound.

A single Pickler writing one logical stream into a bounded counting sink would preserve memo identity while measuring serialized length; split storage chunks do not inherently change pickle memo semantics if produced by one Pickler and reassembled in order.

concrete_gaps_before_new_experiment.finding: Pickle is executable during deserialization. A matching hash alone is not provenance or safety if the expected hash/manifest can be supplied by an untrusted party. Future loading must be restricted to locally generated bytes under an authenticated, immutable completion receipt and a trusted environment; never load partial or externally supplied pickle. Source/runtime pins do not make arbitrary pickle safe.

The counting-sink proposal validates only byte count/hash for the serialized stream, not that it can be restored or that shared graph identities survive the proposed chunk/manifest reader. A separately bounded restore test on a completed, trusted stream is required before treating chunk layout as usable.

The new proposal itself does not store or validate a numerical full 662-gradient vector or point. Its prose correctly leaves numerical persistence separate. Before numerical claims, preserve complete ordered point arrays, all 662 coordinates with names/shapes/dtypes/offsets, full vector and scalar density before later assertions, then independently compare/parity check.

The parent-envelope claim is specific to the pinned first-parent contract. It does not establish another parent's identity, row, exposure, mass or target. Any future cross-parent reuse needs a separate authenticated complete-parent envelope; no mass or all-parent normalization can be inferred from this serialized graph.

The 16 MiB report/cache and 512 MiB stream budgets require synchronous pre-write enforcement and counting of all partial chunks/metadata; a periodic watchdog alone can overshoot. A disk-headroom recheck should include the retained old 64 MiB partial file and concurrent filesystem use.

failure_interpretation: The symbolic graph passed recorded structural checks; persistence failed at the per-file cap. It is neither a failed gradient derivation nor successful complete persistence. Numerical equivalence, lineage beyond the explicit-input tripwire, restorability, normalization and scientific qualification remain unestablished.
recommendation: A fresh independently reviewed, resource-bounded counting-sink run is technically reviewable as measurement only. Require exact source/receipt/resource pins, a new attempt directory, a strict write-budget sink and failure manifest; do not revise or load the existing partial. Consider chunk persistence only after exact size is known and a separate restore design is reviewed.
